title: Solution
description: Structured format for a solution proposed by the solution-generator skill.

title.description: Short, action-oriented title (≤ 80 chars). Start with an imperative verb.
examples: Repair and upgrade water distribution network in eastern district

description.description: 1–3 sentence narrative explaining the solution approach, why it works, and who benefits.
examples: Replace the ageing cast-iron pipes in the eastern district with corrosion-resistant PVC pipes and install a real-time leak detection system. The upgrade will eliminate the recurring pipe bursts that have caused water outages for 180,000 residents. Implementation will be phased to keep at least 50% of supply online at all times.

steps.description: Ordered list of concrete implementation steps. Each step starts with an imperative verb and names the responsible actor where possible.
examples: Deploy emergency water tankers to affected neighbourhoods within 24 hours (city water authority).
Conduct a full pipe condition survey across the eastern district within 2 weeks (engineering contractor).
Issue a public tender for pipe replacement works targeting completion within 6 months.
Install IoT-based pressure and flow sensors at 20 key junctions for real-time monitoring.
Establish a 24/7 leak response team with a 2-hour SLA for burst pipe incidents.

difficulty.description: Implementation difficulty using the feasibility checklist rubric.

estimated_cost.description: Rough cost range including currency symbol and time horizon. Null if genuinely unknown.

expected_impact.description: Quantified or clearly qualified outcome after full implementation.
examples: Eliminate water outages for 180,000 residents; reduce pipe burst incidents by ~80% within 12 months of completion.

short_term_action.description: The single most important immediate action (0–30 days) before the full solution is deployed.
examples: Deploy 20 water tankers to serve affected households within 48 hours.
